- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from 14d avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent high for next 5d.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model underreacts; add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion in early 30d horizon; for 1–7d ahead, use 1.5x smoothing of recent 7d average.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model tends to lag; add 0.2–0.5% upward bias for 1–3d ahead.
- For 10–30d horizon, model underestimates downward trends; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias if sentiment is negative and price has fallen >1.5% in last 7d.
